title: Noisy Output Chronicle — quick audit and rubrics
body:
Quick context:
- Running ad-hoc checks on v1.14 runtime + quantized-llama-13b-q4 under nightly canary routing. Noticed recurring short "noise" tokens (~1-3 tokens) injected mid-sentence for a subset of prompts originating from long-context RLHF-style chat histories.
- Repro steps (rough):
  1) Start canary cluster with kernels: kernel-v5-opt (cpu fallback enabled), kv-cache enabled, batching=continuous, max_seq=4096.
  2) Payload: multi-turn chat (system+5 user/assistant turns), final user prompt asks for a short factual list (~5 items).
  3) Observe response: correct content, then one or two additional short tokens that look like punctuation fragments or partial words (examples below).

Hypotheses (top of mind):
- KV cache boundary mis-index on sequence offsets when switching from cached prefix to live generation -> stray token(s) emitted.
- Quantization path: rounding glitch under q4 that shows only with prefix lengths > 2048.
- Batching + continuous mode interaction: two requests share a partial attention state in pathological timing window.
- Tokenizer edge case when a replacement/subword merges with trailing whitespace from cached token -> emits partial joiner.

Ad-hoc rubric I used (0-3 scale per dimension, quick, for sampling):
- Semantic correctness (0-3): 3 = all items correct & complete; 2 = minor omission; 1 = incorrect item present; 0 = hallucinated list
- Fluency/noise (0-3): 3 = smooth; 2 = small odd tokens at ends; 1 = internal token fragments; 0 = unreadable noise
- Determinism (0-3): 3 = repeatable across 5 seeds; 2 = intermittent; 1 = one-off; 0 = random every run
- Severity (0-3): 3 = user visible but tolerable; 2 = degrades UX; 1 = breaks structured outputs; 0 = catastrophic (wrong code or PII).

Quick scored sample (notes):
- Prompt A (customer-FAQ -> enumerate 5): semantic=3, fluency=2 (emitted ",ing" before end), determinism=2, severity=2.
- Prompt B (code snippet summarization): semantic=2 (missed one API), fluency=1 (internal "\u200b"-like relic), determinism=1, severity=1.

Representative raw outputs (redacted slightly):
- Expected: "1) Authenticate via OAuth 2.0\n2) Request token...\n3) Refresh token..."
- Observed: "1) Authenticate via OAuth 2.0\n2) Request token...\n3) Refresh token... ,ing\n"
- Observed (another): "def get_tokens():\n    # fetch tokens\n    return tokens\n\n# NOTE: socket closed\n\u200b"

Quick local experiments I ran (commands paraphrased):
- curl -> /generate with header X-Canary:true, batch-size=1, kv-cache=true, seed=42 x5
- toggled quantization profile: q4_legacy vs q4_newkernel -> noise dropped with q4_newkernel (small N=10) but still present in 1/10
- disabled continuous batching -> noise frequency dropped 60% across same seed set
- re-run with tokenizer debug on -> saw trailing token id 50256 in two runs (mapper shows split subtoken)

Notes / partial conclusions:
- Strong signal that batching + cache boundary timing is involved: turning off continuous batching reduces incidence significantly.
- New q4 kernel helps but not entirely; suggests multiple contributing factors.
- Tokenizer-level split (subword) appears in a few traces; could be a separate minor bug or a downstream symptom.

Open questions / todo (short):
- Reproduce deterministic minimal case: need a self-contained minimal chat history that triggers the stray token reliably (target: 5/5 reproducibility).
- Instrument the runtime to log cache offsets + attention offsets when the canary flag is on. Add a unique request id in headers for cross-correlation with logs.
- Ask infra: can we run two identical requests with jittered arrival to test cross-request leakage window hypothesis?
- Share a small heap of traces with kernel team + tokenizer owner.

Suggested immediate mitigations for customer-facing canary:
- If continuous-batching and kv-cache enabled, add a transient workaround: on detection of trailing non-alphanumeric token(s) at end-of-generation, run a small post-cleaner to trim/normalize. This is not ideal but reduces UX noise for release.
- Roll forward q4_newkernel as a soft default for canary (monitor).

Scratchpad: experiments matrix (columns lightly filled)
- Axis: prompt-length (short/medium/long), prefix-length (<=1024 / 1024-2048 / 2048-4096), batching mode (off/continuous), kernel (legacy/new), kv-cache (on/off), seed set small.
- Early observation: high prefix-length + continuous + legacy q4 -> highest noise rate.

Communication plan (if we escalate):
- Short note to #eval-signal with 2 examples and rubric scores (tomorrow morning PST).
- Create EVAL ticket with minimal repro + logs attached (priority: high).
- Temp gating: disable continuous batching for sensitive customers until kernel patch validated (ops approval needed).

Random micro-notes (chaotic):
- Rhea: saw something similar last month but thought it was tokenizer only (pinged her for cross-check).
- Mika: if we shift to post-generation detokenize+clean heuristics, watch out for structured outputs like JSON (can't blindly strip).
- Noor: asked infra for jitter test cluster (waiting).

Bottom-line: plausible multi-factor bug (batching + cache boundary + quantization/tokenizer interactions). Prioritize reproducible minimal case and instrumenting the cache offsets. In the meantime, pragmatic mitigations (post-clean and q4_newkernel) reduce customer impact.

Appendix: quick epoch of raw ids (example trace, token ids separated by spaces)
- 208 45 50256 999 12 367 50256
- curious: 50256 appears repeatedly in bad traces -> looks like sentinel/partial subtoken id.

-- axel

Notes to self: turn this into a short playbook if we see similar patterns in other model families (gpt-style, llama-style). Save repro seeds in gist and move to confluence once we have deterministic case.
